# 1 Enoch Chapter 99 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QEn (Aramaic) | **Section:** Epistle of Enoch — Woe Oracles

---

**1** Woe to you who act impiously and praise and honor lying words; you shall perish and shall not have a good life.

**2** Woe to those who pervert the words of uprightness, transgress the eternal law, and transform themselves into what they were not; they shall be trodden underfoot upon the earth.

**3** In those days, make ready, you righteous, to lift your prayers as a memorial and place them as a testimony before the angels, that they may present the sin of sinners as a memorial before the Most High.

**4** In those days the nations shall be stirred up, and the families of the nations shall arise on the day of destruction.

**5** And in those days the destitute shall go out and carry off their children, and shall abandon them, so that their children shall perish through them; yes, they shall abandon their children who are still nursing and not return to them, and shall have no love for their beloved ones.

**6** And again I swear to you, sinners, that sin is prepared for a day of unceasing bloodshed.

**7** And those who worship stones and images of gold and silver and wood and stone and clay, and those who worship impure spirits and demons and all kinds of idols not according to knowledge — they shall get no help from them whatsoever.

**8** And they shall become godless because of the folly of their hearts, and their eyes shall be blinded through the fear of their hearts and through visions in their dreams.

**9** Through these things they shall become godless and fearful, for they shall have done all their work in a lie and worshipped stone; therefore they shall perish in an instant.

**10** But in those days blessed are all they who accept the words of wisdom, understand them, observe the paths of the Most High, walk in the path of His righteousness, and do not become godless with the godless; for they shall be saved.

**11** Woe to you who spread evil to your neighbors, for you shall be slain in Sheol.

**12** Woe to you who make deceitful and false measures, and to those who cause bitterness on the earth; for they shall thereby be utterly consumed.

**13** Woe to those who build their houses not with their own labor, and all their building materials are bricks and stones of sin; I tell you: you shall have no peace.

**14** Woe to those who reject the measure and eternal heritage of their fathers and cause their souls to follow after idols; for they shall have no rest.

**15** Woe to those who work unrighteousness and help oppression and slay their neighbors until the day of the great judgment.

**16** For He will cast down your glory and bring affliction on your hearts, and He will arouse His fierce indignation and destroy you all with the sword; and all the holy and righteous shall remember your sins.

---

*LOGOS notes: V. 3 introduces the motif of prayers as heavenly memorial — a liturgical act that becomes a legal testimony before the angels. V. 5 depicts apocalyptic social breakdown: nursing infants abandoned by their own parents. V. 10 is a solitary beatitude breaking the relentless woe cycle. V. 13 targets those who build with exploited labor — the strongest statement in the woe cycle against economic oppression through construction. Cf. Jeremiah 22:13: "Woe to him who builds his palace by unrighteousness."*
